side_letters.title: MFN — Strategic Investor (Series B)
side_letters.summary: MFN clause grants the Series B strategic investor the right to elect any more-favorable economic terms granted to a subsequent investor. The clause is broad-but-undefined; specific scope must be confirmed with counsel.
side_letters.body: Section 4.1 (Most-Favored-Nation). If the Company issues equity securities to any subsequent investor on terms more favorable in the aggregate than the terms set forth in the Series B Stock Purchase Agreement (including without limitation any preferred return rate, anti-dilution variant, redemption right, conversion ratio adjustment, board observer right, or information right), the Investor shall have the right, upon written notice within thirty (30) days of receiving disclosure of such issuance, to elect to substitute the more-favorable terms for the corresponding terms in this Agreement on a clause-by-clause basis. The Investor may elect to apply this MFN right selectively (i.e., adopting some but not all more-favorable terms).
unresolved_questions: Does the MFN cover anti-dilution variant, or only economic preference terms?
Is the 30-day notice window measured from issuance, from disclosure, or from closing?
Does 'more favorable in the aggregate' permit clause-by-clause cherry-picking, or only whole-package election?
